result.title: VAPOR: Improving Multimodal Reasoning with Sparse Visual Updates
result.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made substantial progress in visual reasoning, but extended generation over large visual contexts remains computationally expensive. During autoregressive decoding, visual attention is recomputed for every generated token, even when consecutive tokens rely on similar visual evidence. We introduce VAPOR (Visual Attention Persistence with On-demand Refresh), a training-free framework that reduces this redundancy by reusing visual attention outputs across decoding steps and refreshing them when needed. VAPOR caches the visual attention output while continuing to update textual attention at every step, helping reduce visual grounding drift during extended reasoning. To decide when to reuse cached outputs, VAPOR estimates visual attention mass using a low-rank approximation. It also uses prefill-based attention consistency and cache age to make independent Persist and Refresh decisions for each attention head. VAPOR retains the full visual key-value (KV) cache, so all visual tokens remain available when new evidence is needed. Experiments on eight image and four video reasoning benchmarks across two MLLM families show that VAPOR improves accuracy over dense attention on nearly all benchmarks while achieving 1.11-1.21x decoding speedups. Compared with the strongest state-of-the-art acceleration baseline in each setting, VAPOR further improves accuracy by 0.35-2.15 percentage points while achieving comparable or lower decoding latency. Our code is available at https://github.com/Su-my/VAPOR.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的 VAPOR 框架：在多模态自回归解码中缓存视觉注意力输出、每步仍更新文本注意力，并用低秩近似估计视觉注意力质量、结合 prefill 一致性与缓存年龄，为每个注意力头独立决定「复用或刷新」，同时保留完整视觉 KV。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把「何时重新读取视觉证据」变成可度量的逐头决策，直接对应 LOOK 类收益与成本权衡、长推理中的视觉 grounding drift，以及 latent/缓存相似度受深度、位置与注意力结构影响的问题，可供核查其决策信号能否迁移到 latent 状态的视觉证据筛选。
